commits.message:
Delete the L1 control-plane source scans and bundle worker probes outside the package

Midgard Node CI on e71c6d22c failed in l1-control-plane-deleted.test.ts:
its scan of the node sources found the esbuild bundle that
intent-journal-worker-holds.test.ts was writing into the package root at
the same moment. Tests that scan source text or census the tree are
deleted when they go red, so that test goes, together with its docs
counterpart and the key list only those two read.

The two worker-thread tests now bundle their probe through one helper
that writes into the system temporary directory, with the package's
node_modules linked beside the bundle so its external imports still
resolve. No tree walk can find a probe bundle mid-run, and the copied
bundling setup lives in one place.

Build the stack drill on the confirmed state when every block has merged

On an idle stack our node merges each attested block once it matures,
whoever holds the shift, so the state queue can hold only its root. The
drill read its predecessor, appended its blocks and checked its correction
evidence as if the queue always held a block, and twin4-long-2 failed at
its first family reading an empty queue.

A commit on an empty queue spends the root, and its header continues the
root's confirmed state (state-queue.ak:1157-1191, :124-138); a merge
writes the merged block's hash, UTxO root and end time into the root
(:401-409). So the drill now:

- reads the root as the settled, attested tail, rebuilding the block it
  holds from the authenticated transaction whose output the merge spent;
- appends after a block that merged by anchoring on the root, re-read at
  every commit attempt, in staging and in the transition trace;
- treats a block that left the queue by an authenticated merge as kept,
  in the predecessor, successor and removal-tail evidence;
- reads an attested history block that merged between polls as attested,
  and fails by name on a fault that merged before its fraud proof.

Forget a removal's backoff and warning when the bridge stops driving it

A finished correction clears its backoff, now pinned by a test: a later
failure retries at once and warns again. The bridge also drops the
asset's warned failure when it stops finishing that correction, so the
map no longer only shrinks on a settled removal.

Refs #921

Type the watcher's wallet holds from one signature

The funding store's holdWalletInputs takes the fault-proofs
HoldWalletInputs type, and WatcherWalletLeases names the store view the
application and the bridge share.

Refs #921

Hold a proven removal's coins until its transaction's TTL

The hold now ends when the signed removal can no longer land, read from
its TTL, rather than a fresh wall-clock window, so a caller's later
validTo cannot outlive it. A test pins that a failed removal keeps its
holds, as its last transaction may still land.

Refs #921

Drop the local-finalization fields from commit worker test inputs

Deleting block confirmation removed availableLocalFinalizationBlock and
localFinalizationPending from the commit worker's input, and the
candidate-input validator now requires the exact remaining key set.
The candidate-probe artifact test still built its input with both, so
four of its cases failed on the key check. Remove them there and from
the three other test inputs that still carried them.

Refs #806

Move the SDK/Aiken schema parity test into the SDK

The parity test now sits next to the schemas it checks, in
demo/midgard-sdk/tests/sdk-aiken-schema-parity.test.ts. The node copy
and its ci-file-durations entry are gone, so exactly one table remains.

ABI_MAPPINGS becomes MIRRORS: an object from SDK export name to Aiken
definition. Its keys are typed against the SDK's exports, so renaming
a schema without the table fails typecheck. The 39 rows are unchanged
and each still has to refine its definition, field titles included.

The comments that explained missing rows become NO_BLUEPRINT_DEFINITION.
Each entry names the Aiken definition the blueprint does not publish,
what pins the encoding instead, and a one-line reason. There are six:
- ValidationTraceDescriptor: the transition-trace-abi channel;
- MidgardTxValidity: VALIDITY_VECTORS, which moved with the test;
- CaseConfig: validation-case-v1.test.ak;
- LostDefenseReceipt: operator-lost-defense-slash.test.ak;
- ValidationAuxiliaryWitness: the validation-auxiliary-witness-v1
  channel;
- ValidationProofItemDatum: the validation-one-step-cross-language
  channel.
The list is shrink-only. An entry fails once the blueprint gains its
definition, and also when its pin is neither a golden channel, an
existing repository path nor VALIDITY_VECTORS. The entry count is
pinned at six.

The comments about rows that were red pending #579 regeneration are
dropped, because those rows have been green for some time.

Refs #917

Back off retries of a failed proven-record removal

The fault decision bridge started a failed removal again on every
dispatching pass and warned on each failure. Retries now follow a
backoff per fraud-proof asset name, from 1 s doubling to 60 s, on the
bridge's monotonic clock, and a failure is warned only when it first
happens or its message changes. A confirmed removal or a finished
correction clears the backoff.

Closes #921

Hold a proven removal's wallet coins until it confirms

At its pre-submit boundary, the proven-record removal now holds the
signed transaction's wallet inputs and collateral in the funding store
until its validity window ends, and releases the hold once the removal
confirms. A rejected removal leaves its hold to expire. If a coin is
already leased or held, the attempt fails before anything is submitted.

Only coins at the prover wallet address are held: script inputs belong
to no reservation, and holding them would make a retried removal
conflict with its own earlier hold.

The watcher passes the removal one walletLeases dependency, the store's
readReservedOutRefs and holdWalletInputs, in place of the separate
reserved out-ref readers.

Refs #921

Let the funding store hold wallet coins outside a reservation

A proven-record removal spends prover-wallet coins (its fee input and
collateral) that no funding reservation leases, so a reservation plan
built while the removal is unconfirmed can select the same coin and the
two transactions race for it.

Add holdWalletInputs to the prover funding reservation store. A hold
lives in memory until its wall-clock expiry or its release, and a
restart drops every hold. Holding a coin that is leased or already held
throws ReservationConflictError and takes nothing. readReservedOutRefs
now also returns live holds, and reserving a held coin conflicts.

Refs #921

Check every registered step datum against its validator's blueprint datum

The registry now drives a conformance test. For each family definition
REGISTERED_FAMILY_DEFINITIONS derives from FAMILY_APPLICATION_REGISTRY,
stepDatumSchemas[i] is paired with step contract i
(familyStepContractNames), that contract's validator title
(deploymentValidatorTitle), and the validator's datum definition in the
blueprint. Each pair is checked with refines(). No schema is declared
anew. Every lookup throws rather than skipping a step.

That gives 361 pairs over the 47 registered families:
- 158 refine;
- 202 declare their step with FraudProofComputationThreadStepDatum,
  whose thread state is opaque Data;
- min_ada step_04 adds a never-emitted second state arm, because Lucid
  collapses a one-constructor enum to void.

The last two groups are seeded into a shrink-only allowance list keyed
by validator title: 79 opaque-state titles and one min-ada title. Each
entry gives a one-line reason and the exact report it permits. A pair
whose report differs fails, including one that starts to refine. So
does an entry no registered step reaches. The entry count is pinned
at 80.

Two permanent negatives cover mistakes made at declaration:
- min-ada's step datums declared out of order are caught at both
  misplaced steps;
- a mis-titled envelope field is caught with its blueprint title.

Refs #917

Check SDK schemas against the blueprint by refinement

sdk-aiken-schema-parity compared each SDK schema with its blueprint
definition after normalising titles away. Two same-typed fields
swapped in a TypeScript schema therefore passed. Swap normalizeSchema
for refines on the same 39 ABI_MAPPINGS rows, so constructor field
titles and their order are now checked too. Add a negative test:
HeaderSchema with withdrawal_count and deposit_count, both Int,
swapped is reported at both fields.

refines compares recursive definitions coinductively. Correct the
notes that blamed recursion for the missing ValidationAuxiliaryWitnessV1
row: no validator declares it in its ABI, so the blueprint has no
definition to check it against. The notes are in the parity test, the
one-step fixture generator and the HeaderV1 ABI step of Node CI.

Refs #917

Move blueprint readers onto the SDK blueprint ABI reader

Move parseExactAikenDataCbor from @al-ft/midgard-fault-proofs into
@al-ft/midgard-sdk/blueprint-abi and drop its fault-proofs root
export. It now resolves definitions through the reader and shares its
opaque-Data predicate, so an opaque alias of Data (description "Any
Plutus data.") accepts any Plutus Data. Its callers in
midgard-validation import it from the subpath, and its test moves to
the SDK.

Delete the test-support readers it replaces:
- fault-proofs tests/support/blueprint-abi.ts; its callers read
  constructors through parseBlueprintAbi.
- midgard-node's header-fixture definition, constructor, constructors
  and fields helpers; the tests read the same data through the
  reader.
- midgard-validation's spendRedeemerDefinitionName, which had no
  callers.

verify-canonical-v1-header-v1-abi.mjs already runs after the SDK
build. It now reads the blueprint through the built subpath. Its
self-test pins the reader's refusal for a missing HeaderV1
definition.

Refs #917

Add the blueprint ABI reader subpath to the SDK

Add @al-ft/midgard-sdk/blueprint-abi, one pure reader of a compiled
Aiken blueprint. parseBlueprintAbi parses validators eagerly and
resolves definitions on lookup; it throws on a missing title, a
missing definition or any $ref that is not a #/definitions/<name>
pointer. refines(ts, ref) lists every place a TypeScript Data schema
fails to refine a blueprint definition, comparing snake-normalised
constructor field titles and order, constructor indices, arity and
shapes, and treating a recursive definition coinductively.

Re-implement parseFaultProofBlueprint and assertParameterShapes over
the reader, with the same exports. The blueprint shape refusals drop
their "Fault proof" prefix, and a parameter, datum or redeemer schema
that is not a definitions pointer or an object is now refused at
parse time.

The subpath is wired like the existing ones: package exports,
publishConfig and the tsup entry. A static module-graph test holds it
to its own directory.

Refs #917

Drop the size exception for the deposit-flow commit-selection test

The deposit-flow emulator rework left the file at 456 lines, under the
500-line limit.
